title: Hit List: inspect candidates with an explicit companion window
description: Use unchanged Regression results to explore real Hit List filters and exports, while explicitly working around the hidden native panel.
objectives: Distinguish the broken native shortcut from the external companion.
Interpret ranked candidates without claiming significant discoveries.
Filter, restore and export the actual result rows.
prerequisite: Extract Hit_List_real_results_companion.zip. Activate your spaCR environment and run python hit_list_companion.py, then Browse to results. The companion wraps the unmodified HitListScreen; it does not repair Regression navigation or wire Investigate. The archive contains original Regression outputs, not a full project. There are 325 genes, 434 guide rows and zero genes passing q <= .05. Effects are standardized marginal effects, not simultaneous multivariable coefficients. Missing intervals are unavailable. Exported n_obs=0 does not report actual well support: use results_gene.csv wells_with_gene, which ranges from 2 to 48. Metadata joins, penalised ranking and Investigate are outside this demonstration. No model training, new regression, GPU or AI-provider request is needed. API: spacr.hits.build_hit_list and HitList.filter/write_csv/to_markdown/to_html.

scenes.narration: Hit List belongs under Regression. In this build, clicking Hits selects a page inside a hidden panel, so the list does not appear. This tutorial shows that limitation openly. The following window is an external companion, not evidence that the native shortcut has been repaired.

Extract the linked example, activate your spaCR environment, and run the bundled Hit List companion script. The labelled companion opens spaCR's existing Hit List widget without changing its calculations. Click Browse and select the extracted results folder. No regression is rerun, and Investigate integration is not connected here.

The original example loads three hundred twenty-five genes. Double-click column boundaries if values are clipped. Read effect direction, raw P, corrected q and guide agreement separately. Missing confidence intervals are unavailable. These are standardized marginal effects; the exported observation-count zero is not the true number of supporting wells.

Set Max q to zero point zero five. No genes remain because the smallest gene q-value is about zero point two seven one. An empty filtered table is not an import failure. Restore Max q to one to recover all candidates; this does not declare them discoveries.

Minimum guides two keeps one hundred seventeen genes with at least two tested guide rows. This counts available evidence, not every guide originally designed for a library. The filter changes the displayed subset without recomputing the original multiple-testing correction.

Minimum agreement one additionally keeps fifty-seven genes whose tested guides all share the gene effect's sign. Agreement is not proof of significance or causality. The summary still reports zero significant corroborated genes, even though these candidate rows have agreeing guides.

Hide controls removes one control row, leaving fifty-six candidates in this subset. Restore it before the later export. Removing controls from view does not refit the model or change the correction family; retain their identities when interpreting your analysis.

With the other filters cleared, Direction up shows positive effects. Adding a minimum absolute effect of zero point one leaves sixteen rows here. These are illustrative display choices, not recommended thresholds. Restore direction and effect controls before searching or comparing a different subset.

Search a recorded identifier to inspect one real row. An unmatched query gives an empty table; returning to the known identifier restores it, and clearing search restores the population. This demonstrates reversible filtering. Annotation imports and the separate Investigate workflow require their own checks.

For export, restore two guides, full agreement, controls included and an empty search. All three exports contain the same fifty-seven candidates in this example. Markdown and HTML round numbers; CSV preserves numerical detail. Save the filter choices separately, because the files do not record every setting.

Clear the filters to recover all three hundred twenty-five genes. Keep exported subsets separate from unchanged originals and do not label nonsignificant candidates as validated hits. Python offers the same Hit List reader and filters, but check the format-specific row limits when exporting larger lists.
